slides.label: Closing costs
slides.headline: The price isn't *the whole cheque*.
slides.body: New-build closing costs run higher than resale, because the builder passes through items a private seller never charges.

slides.label: Budget roughly
slides.headline: of the purchase price.
slides.body: About $30,000 to $45,000 on a $1.1M freehold home outside Toronto.

slides.label: What's in it
slides.headline: Land transfer tax, *levies*, hookups, Tarion enrolment, legal.
slides.body: Plus grading deposits and tax adjustments. Inside Toronto, add roughly $18,000 in municipal land transfer tax.

slides.label: The ones that run
slides.headline: Uncapped levies and *a failed rebate*.
slides.body: Development charges can rise with no ceiling unless capped. A net-of-rebate price you don't qualify for can add up to $80,000.

caption:
Closing day costs more than the price on the agreement. 🧾

📊 Budget roughly 2% to 4% of the price
🏛️ Land transfer tax, levies, utility hookups, Tarion enrolment and legal fees
⚠️ Uncapped development charges can keep rising until closing

slides.label: Myth vs fact
slides.headline: Myth: freehold buyers get *10 days to cancel* too.
slides.body: The 10-day right comes from the Condominium Act. A freehold home falls outside it, so no equivalent right exists.

caption:
Condo buyers get 10 days. Freehold buyers don't. 👀

🏢 The 10-day rescission right comes from the Condominium Act
🏡 Detached, semis and freehold towns fall outside that Act
✍️ On freehold, your protection has to be built in before you sign
⚖️ Lawyer review first, signature second

slides.headline: Your mortgage is approved *at closing*, not at signing.
slides.body: Income, rates and the appraised value are re-tested a few months out. An appraisal gap is cash on closing day.

caption:
Signing today, funding years from now. 🏦

📋 Lenders underwrite 3 to 6 months before closing, on that day's facts
📉 They lend on the lesser of price and appraised value
💵 Any appraisal gap is yours to cover in cash
🛡️ Buy below your maximum and keep a reserve
